What the consolidated file shows

The book runs across 754 health systems and 8,161 accounts — 1,605 360 current, 840 360 target, 5,511 transactional — carrying $3,715,618 of portal balance against a $18,222,000 2026 budget across 154 systems.

Concentration is heavy: the top 10 systems hold $2.20M, or 59% of portal balance. Partner earnings of $34.72M are the engine; redemptions against them total −$23.33M across cash, equipment, parts, services and training.

21 systems with 267 accounts and $616K of escrow are operating without a signed 360 agreement. Purely transactional systems need no 360 agreement and are marked N/A.

Customer-side coverage trails internal coverage: 116 systems have a named authorized redeemer and 85 a 360 disposition champion, leaving 58 with live 360 accounts and no redeemer on file. 5 systems have no named reLink sell-to coordinator.

Before this becomes the system of record

Data gaps and method

Two role vocabularies, deliberately kept apart

Acquisition coordinator and sell-to coordinator are internal reLink owners, from the account hierarchy export. Authorized redeemer and 360 disposition champion are customer-side contacts, from the contact roles export — the champion is stored in Salesforce as “360 Program Champion”. Contacts flagged “no longer there” were dropped. Four contact accounts — CME, Unity Health, BioMedovation and VHC Health — did not match an account in the hierarchy and carry no roll-up.

2026 annual budget is a tracker figure, not a Salesforce field

Budgets come from the 2026 Annual Budget column of the Master Tracker workbook, read across its all-accounts, net-new and strategic sheets — 406 rows collapsing to 168 distinct accounts worth $19,532,000. The same account is often spelled differently sheet to sheet (Jefferson Health / Jefferson; Lurie Childrens / Laurie Childrens), so rows are deduplicated on a normalized key and the highest figure taken, never summed. 154 accounts matched a health system, totalling $18,222,000; the remaining 14 are net-new prospects with no Salesforce account yet, worth $1,310,000. Where a parent legitimately carries several distinct tracker lines they are summed: GE HealthCare rolls up five, Kaiser Permanente two regions.

Open TPS is linked for 360 Current only

Three TPS exports have been merged to 1,367 YTD records, 87 of them open. Account names were supplied for the 360 Current slice, so all 39 of those open records nest under their child account and roll up to 29 health systems. The other 48 open records carry only Queue TPS Seller Account Status, a status value rather than a join key. Adding the Seller Account lookup to that export closes the remainder.

Contract status reads N/A for transactional systems

Only 360 partners need a signed 360 agreement. Systems with no 360 current or 360 target accounts show N/A rather than a contract state; “Unsigned” and “On file” apply only to systems with 360 accounts.

Escrow covers 360 partners only

The escrow report is filtered to reLink 360 Partner = True, so 1,319 accounts carry GL detail. The 5,511 transactional accounts under those same parents are all present in the hierarchy but show no escrow line — a filter boundary, not missing money.

What was excluded, and what reconciles

Every account that rolls up to an ultimate parent is included — 360 current, 360 target and transactional alike. Dropped: eBay, Shopify, Proxibid and auction-channel buyer records, and roughly 55,000 one-off individual buyer accounts with no parent and no escrow. Portal balance ties to the source report exactly at $3,715,618.
